newsitem.title: USA: Expedited appeal denied in Conrail case.
newsitem.headline: Expedited appeal denied in Conrail case.

text.p: A U.S. appeals court Monday denied a Norfolk Southern Corp request for an expedited appeal of a lower court ruling against its attempts to block the planned merger between Conrail Inc and CSX Corp, a court official said.

The U.S. Third Circuit Court of Appeals, however, agreed to consider a request for an injunction, pending resolution of the appeal, blocking a crucial January 17 Conrail shareholders meeting, said the official, reading from the court's order.
The appeals court asked Conrail and CSX to file responses to the Norfolk Southern requestss by noon Eastern time Monday, and Norfolk Southern to file a reply by noon Tuesday.
The appeal contests Thursday's rulings by U.S. District Judge Donald Van Artsdalen against Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern.

Van Artsdalen had denied a Norfolk Southern request for a preliminary injunction against a two-year "no-shop" provision in the CSX-Conrail merger agreement, which prevents Conrail from considering another offer until 1999.

He also rejected Norfolk Southern's argument that Conrail and CSX, of Richmond, Va., triggered a Pennsylvania law that would require CSX to pay all cash for Conrail shares. And he declined to block the January 17 Conrail shareholders meeting until a final legal decision on the issue could be rendered.

At the meeting, shareholders will be asked to waive the Pennsylvania law, which requires that a company acquiring 20 percent or more of the shares in another company must pay "fair value," -- essentially, equivalent terms -- for all the other shares.
Approval of the waiver would allow CSX to close on a $110 per-share cash tender January 22, which would raise its stake in Conrail to 40 percent from 19.9 percent.

At that point, approval of the $9.1 billion merger proposal by Conrail shareholders would be certain because CSX also holds an option on a 15 percent Conrail stake, large enough to give it majority control. CSX intends to swap shares for the remaining 60 percent of Conrail.
Norfolk Southern, pursuing a rival $10.3 billion bid for Conrail, said in its appeal that Van Artsdalen had erred on both the "no-shop" and "fair value" issues.
